title: MYTH BUSTER CONTINUATION — JANUS / Little Lamplight Threshold Cluster
scope: Deepen the JANUS investigation around the shipped Fallout 3 Little Lamplight holotape cluster and adjacent dialogue, while separating literal game evidence from external classical Janus semantics and from human interpretation.

primary_game_objects.name: January 26, 2077 -- Little Lamplight!
primary_game_objects.speaker: unnamed Little Lamplighter; game-file speaker assignment uses young Amata voice
content_summary: The children report that they have been living in the caves for about three months.
Jason is credited with organizing work and cooperation for survival.
The children describe themselves as a whole new city and adopt the name Little Lamplight.
They secretly vote to make Jason the city's first mayor and plan to tell him the next day.

primary_game_objects.name: My diary, by Jason Grant -- entry 1
content_summary: Jason identifies himself as ten years old and a pupil from Early Dawn Elementary.
He says the war destroyed the outside world while the children survived in the caves.
After the adults disappear, he begins assuming responsibility because other children already listen to him.

primary_game_objects.name: My diary, by Jason Grant -- entry 2
content_summary: Nearly two months have passed and the children remain on their own.
Jason explicitly describes a door in the caverns leading to Vault 87.
The children repeatedly bang on the closed door and are refused entry.
After someone inside tells them they are already dead, Jason rejects dependence on adults.

primary_game_objects.name: Joseph's Little Lamplight oral history
content_summary: The children remember the adult world as the world that destroyed itself.
They preserve Little Lamplight through a rule that residents must leave before becoming grown-ups.
Leaving friends behind is treated as necessary to preserve the children's world.
The tradition explicitly frames this as survival until the outside world is rebuilt.

primary_game_objects.name: Happy Birthday to You / Sticky transition
content_summary: Sticky reaches the age at which Little Lamplighters must leave.
The transition is physically enacted by leaving Little Lamplight and traveling toward Big Town.

chronology.jason_entry_1_relative_time: about one month after the Great War
chronology.jason_entry_2_relative_time: almost two months after the Great War
chronology.lamplight_holo05_internal_context: about three months after the Great War
chronology.note: The displayed year 2077 is incompatible with the post-October-2077 three-month context. The evidence supports a likely year typo, not a prophecy or time anomaly.

janus_external_reference.anti_numerology_rule: The day number 26 is not promoted as Janus evidence without an independent historical source.

little_lamplight_janus_mapping.game_evidence: The shipped holotape is explicitly titled January 26, 2077 -- Little Lamplight!
Jason explicitly records a door leading to Vault 87 that the children repeatedly knock on but cannot pass.
little_lamplight_janus_mapping.janus_node: Janus is a guardian of doorways and gateways.

little_lamplight_janus_mapping.game_evidence: After abandonment/refusal by adults, the children define themselves as a whole new city and name it Little Lamplight.
little_lamplight_janus_mapping.janus_node: Janus presides over beginnings and transitions.

little_lamplight_janus_mapping.game_evidence: The January holotape records the secret vote that will install Jason as the city's first mayor.
little_lamplight_janus_mapping.janus_node: Janus is associated with first beginnings and the opening of a new civic cycle.

little_lamplight_janus_mapping.game_evidence: Little Lamplight preserves itself by requiring residents to leave before becoming adults; later gameplay physically stages this transition toward Big Town.
little_lamplight_janus_mapping.janus_node: Janus is associated with thresholds, passages and transitions from one state to another.

little_lamplight_janus_mapping.game_evidence: Joseph's oral history contrasts the world destroyed by adults with survival until the world is rebuilt.
little_lamplight_janus_mapping.janus_node: Janus iconography often faces backward and forward, providing a past/future structural analogy.

jason_name_audit.finding: Jason and Janus are visually similar English spellings but have different classical origins.
jason_name_audit.Jason_classical_etymology: Greek Iason, traditionally associated with healer/healing.
jason_name_audit.Janus_classical_identity: Roman deity of beginnings and doorways/gateways.
jason_name_audit.note: The character name Jason should not be used as evidence for an intended Janus reference without separate developer evidence.

alpha_omega_boundary.literal_referent: Biblical/theological; Catherine's favorite passage and inspiration for Project Purity
alpha_omega_boundary.janus_parallel: The beginning/end polarity is structurally compatible with Janus symbolism.

morse_retest_on_little_lamplight_corpus.method_rule: Morse with removed inter-character timing is used only as a collision test and never as authoritative decoding.

strongest_cluster.interpretation: Within one coherent Little Lamplight narrative cluster, multiple independently real motifs align with Janus domains: January, a literal impassable doorway, a new beginning, first civic leadership, and an enforced life-stage threshold.

claim_ceiling.statement: The artifact preserves a reproducible thematic mapping between real Fallout 3 content and historically documented Janus domains. It does not convert thematic coherence into proof of Bethesda's hidden authorial intent.
